issues: Measurement integrity is fine. The min-max kernel is built from atom-pair counts of train and test SMILES together. This only uses test inputs, never test labels, and each kernel entry depends on just its two molecules, so nothing leaks between rows.

The kernel math is correct for non-negative counts: sum(min) = (sa + sb - L1)/2 and union = sa + sb - sum(min). The slicing is also right: Ktt[np.ix_(tr,tr)] and Ktt[np.ix_(va,tr)] for the inner out-of-fold predictions, and K[n:, :n] for test vs train.

Runtime risk: each fit runs one single-threaded cdist cityblock on about 3360x3360x2048 values (roughly 23e9 operations), which could take about 10-30 s. Over 15 fits that may add several minutes and push the job past the 10-minute limit, depending on how long the incumbent already takes. If it is close, consider sparse min-max or a smaller fpSize.
The diff does not show that Chem, rdFingerprintGenerator and tanimoto are imported or defined in the incumbent. This is assumed, since the candidate passed lint repair.
If any SMILES fails to parse, MolFromSmiles returns None and the kernel step will crash. This is unlikely with the benchmark data.

issues: Integrity is fine. Nothing in the diff reads files, uses pasted values or touches test labels. The QuantileTransformer is fitted only on the training residuals (train_y minus Crippen logP). It is applied to test predictions only through inverse_transform.

No bug makes the result meaningless. The forward and inverse transforms match: the target is multiplied by sd going in and the prediction is divided by sd before inverse_transform. Multiplying by sd changes only the scale, not the model. The stacking meta-learner is fitted and applied in the same transformed space.

Modelling note, not a bug: inverse_transform clips predictions to the range of the training residuals, and back-transforming an averaged prediction from Gaussian space pulls it toward the median. This may limit extrapolation on extreme compounds.

Recomputed z: candidate mean is 0.50055 and incumbent mean is 0.5057, so the improvement is 0.00515. The standard error is sqrt(0.0042²/2 + 0.0042²/2) = 0.0042, which gives z ≈ 1.23. The harness reports 1.221; the gap is probably rounding. This is below a typical significance threshold, so the provisional reject is consistent with the numbers. One option is to run more replicates if the 0.005 gain looks worth confirming.
